Makkan (this surah is Meccan).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} The Exalted glorifies and magnifies His sacred Self, because He possesses great acts and abundant bounties, among which is that He {took His servant} (asrā bi-'abdihi): His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), {from the Sacred Mosque} (al-masjid al-ḥarām), which is the most noble of mosques absolutely, {to the Farthest Mosque} (al-masjid al-aqṣā), which is among the excellent mosques and is the place of the prophets. He made him travel by night to a very distant journey, and he returned in the same night. Allah showed him some of His signs, by which his guidance, insight, steadfastness and discernment increased. This is from His care for him and His kindness, since He facilitated for him the easy path in all his affairs and granted him favours by which he surpassed the first and the last. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the Night Journey (isrā') took place at the beginning of the night and that it began from the Sacred Mosque itself. However, it is established in the Sahih that he was taken from the house of Umm Hani'. According to this, the excellence of the Sacred Mosque extends to the whole of the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram), so that worship is multiplied throughout it just as it is multiplied within the mosque itself. The Night Journey was undertaken with his spirit and body together; otherwise there would be no great sign and no great distinction in it.

Many established hadiths have been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the Night Journey and the description of what he saw in detail: that he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), then he was ascended from there through the heavens until he reached what is above the lofty heavens, and he saw Paradise and Hell, and the prophets in their various ranks. The prayers were prescribed upon him as fifty, and then he kept returning to his Lord, on the advice of Moses the Interlocutor, until they became five in practice and fifty in reward and recompense. On that night he and his community obtained such glories that only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows their extent. Allah mentioned it here, and in the context of the revelation of the Qur'an and the context of the challenge, by the attribute of servanthood, because he attained these great stations by perfecting his servanthood to his Lord.

His saying {Around which We have blessed} (alladhī bārakna ḥawlahu): that is, with an abundance of trees, rivers and perpetual fertility. From its blessing is that it is preferred over other mosques apart from the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Madinah, that travel is undertaken to it for worship and prayer in it, and that Allah has specified it as the place of many of His prophets and chosen ones.

{2} The Creator often pairs the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) with the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him), and their two scriptures with their two laws, because their two scriptures are the most excellent of books, their two laws the most complete of laws, their two prophethoods the highest of prophethoods, and their followers the most numerous of the believers. For this reason He says here: ﴿And We gave Musa the Book﴾, which is the Torah, ﴿and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, by which they would be guided out of the darkness of ignorance to knowledge of the truth. ﴿That you should not take besides Me a trustee (wakil)﴾; that is, We said this to them and sent down the Book to them for this purpose: that they should worship God alone, turn to Him in repentance, and take Him alone as their trustee (wakil) and manager in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, and not depend on other than Him among the creatures, who own nothing and cannot benefit them in anything.

{3} ﴿O offspring of those whom We carried with Noah﴾; that is, O descendants of those upon whom We bestowed favour and whom We carried with Noah. ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾. In this there is a commendation of Noah (peace be upon him) for his giving thanks to God and his being characterised by that, and an exhortation to his descendants to follow his example in gratitude and to imitate him in it, and to remember God's favour upon them in that He preserved them, made them successors on the earth, and drowned others.

{4} ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾; that is, We foretold and covenanted with them, and informed them in their Book, that they would certainly commit corruption on the earth twice, through the commission of sins, insolence toward the blessings of God, exaltation on the earth, and arrogance therein. And that when one of these two occurred, God would give power over them to their enemies and would take vengeance upon them. This is a warning to them and an admonition, so that perhaps they would return and be mindful.

{5} ﴿So when the promise of the first of them comes﴾; that is, the first of the two times in which they would corrupt; that is, when that corruption occurs from them, ﴿We sent against you﴾ servants of Ours by a divine decree, and We gave them power over you by an universal, retributive empowerment, ﴿servants of Ours of great might﴾; that is, possessors of courage, numbers and equipment. So God gave them victory over you, and they killed you, took your children captive, plundered your wealth, and ﴿went through the homes﴾ (jasu khilal al-diyar), meaning they demolished the houses, entered the Sacred Mosque and corrupted it. ﴿And it was a promise fulfilled﴾; it had to occur, because its cause existed among them. The commentators differed about the identity of these empowered people, but they agreed that they were disbelieving people, either from the people of Iraq, or the Jazirah, or elsewhere, whom God empowered over the Children of Israel when sins had multiplied among them, they had abandoned much of their law, and they had transgressed on the earth.

{6} ﴿Then We gave you the return over them﴾; that is, over those who were empowered over you, and you expelled them from your homes. ﴿And We aided you with wealth and sons﴾; that is, We increased your provision, multiplied you, and strengthened you against them. ﴿And We made you greater in manpower﴾ than them; and that was because of your good conduct and your submission to God.

{7} ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves﴾, because the benefit returns to you even in this world, as you witnessed in your victory over your enemies. ﴿And if you do evil, it is against yourselves﴾; that is, the harm returns to your own selves, as God showed you through the empowerment of enemies. ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾; that is, the second time in which you would corrupt on the earth, We would again empower enemies over you, ﴿to distress your faces﴾ through their victory over you and their taking you captive, ﴿and to enter the mosque as they entered it the first time﴾; and by the mosque is meant the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with complete destruction﴾; that is, to ruin and destroy what they gained control of (ma 'alaw 'alayhi), ﴿with complete destruction﴾, so they would ruin your houses, your mosques and your fields.

{8} ﴿Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, by giving you back the upper hand over them. He showed them mercy, granted them dominion, and threatened them for their sins, saying: ﴿And if you return﴾ to corruption on the earth, ﴿We will return﴾ to punishing you. So they returned to it, and God empowered over them His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and God took vengeance upon them through him. This is the reward of this world; but what is with God of punishment is greater and more grievous. For this reason He says: ﴿And We have made Hell for the disbelievers a prison﴾ (hasir); they will burn in it and remain in it, never to leave it. In these verses there is a warning to this Ummah against committing sins, lest there befall them what befell the Children of Israel. The way of God is one; it is not changed or altered. Whoever considers the empowerment of disbelievers over Muslims and over the oppressors will know that this is because of their sins, as a punishment for them; and that when they establish the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, He will establish them firmly on the earth and give them victory over their enemies.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verse 18–21:

{18} He, exalted is He, informs that {whoever desires} the {hastening} (al-'ajilah), that is, the transient, perishing worldly life, and so works and strives for it, forgetting the beginning and the end: Allah hastens to him of its trash and its goods whatever he wishes and desires, of what Allah has decreed for him in the Preserved Tablet. But it is a enjoyment that is neither beneficial nor lasting for him. Then in the Hereafter He will make for him {Hell, which he will burn in}; that is, he will directly experience its punishment, {disgraced and rejected}; that is, in a state of humiliation, disgrace, and reproach from Allah and from His creation, and distance from the mercy of Allah. Thus He combines for him punishment and disgrace.

{19} {And whoever desires the Hereafter}: he is pleased with it and prefers it over the world, {and strives for it with the striving due to it}: the striving to which the heavenly Books and the prophetic traditions call, so he works accordingly to the extent of his ability, {while he is a believer}: in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. {Those, their striving is appreciated}; that is, accepted, recorded and stored up for them, and for them is their reward and recompense with their Lord.

{20} Despite this, their share of the world does not escape them; for each of them Allah provides from it, because it is His gift and His kindness. {And the gift of your Lord is not restricted}; that is, not withheld from anyone, but rather all creation enjoys His bounty and His kindness.

{21} {See how We have favored some of them over others}: in the world, by the abundance and scarcity of provision, ease and hardship, knowledge and ignorance, intellect and foolishness, and other matters by which Allah has favored some servants over others. {And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction}: there is no comparison between the pleasures of this world and its delights and the Hereafter in any respect. How great is the difference between one who is in the lofty chambers, with varied pleasures, joy, goodness and delights, and one who writhes in Hellfire, tormented with painful punishment, upon whom the wrath of the Merciful Lord has descended. And each of the two abodes, among their people, contains a degree of difference that no one can count.

{22} That is: do not believe that any of the created beings deserves any part of worship, and do not associate anyone with Allah. For that is a cause of blame and abandonment. Allah, His angels and His messengers have all forbidden shirk (associating partners with Allah), and have censured those who commit it with the utmost censure. They have attached to it blameworthy names and abhorrent attributes, so that the one who engages in it becomes the most despicable of creatures in description and the most repulsive in quality. And the one who commits it suffers abandonment (khidhlan) in matters of his religion and his worldly life in proportion to what he has forsaken of attachment to his Lord. Whoever attaches himself to other than Allah is forsaken, having been left to the one to whom he attached himself. No one among the creation benefits anyone except by the permission of Allah. Just as the one who sets up another god alongside Allah deserves blame and abandonment, so the one who affirms Allah's oneness, sincerely devotes his religion to Allah, and attaches himself to Him alone, is praiseworthy and aided in all his circumstances.

He is the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, the Repeller of all calamities, the Creator, the Provider, the Governor of all affairs. He alone is singular in all of this, and no other has any share in it. Then, after the right of Him, He mentioned the fulfilment of the right of the parents, saying: {And to parents, good treatment}; that is, treat them well in all the forms of good treatment, in speech and in action, because they are the cause of the servant's existence, and they have a love for the child and kindness toward him, and a closeness that necessitates the affirmation of the right and the obligation of dutiful kindness. {Whether one or both of them reach old age with you}; that is, when they reach this age in which their strength weakens and they need the gentleness and kindness that is well known, {then do not say to them "uff"}: and this is the lowest degree of harm, by which He draws attention to whatever is beyond it; the meaning is: do not harm them even in the slightest way. {And do not scold them}; that is, do not rebuke them or speak to them in a harsh manner. {But speak to them a noble word}: with words they love, and be courteous and gentle with soft, good speech that is pleasing to their hearts and tranquilizes their souls. {31} This is from His mercy toward His servants, for He is more merciful to them than their own parents. He forbade parents to kill their children out of fear of poverty and destitution, and He undertook to provide for all of them. He also informed that: {Killing them is truly a great sin}; that is, it is among the greatest of major sins, because it removes mercy from the heart, constitutes gross disobedience to parents, and is a bold transgression against killing children who have committed no sin or disobedience at all.

{32} The prohibition against approaching it is more emphatic than the prohibition against merely committing it, because that includes prohibiting all its preliminaries and its motivations. For whoever hovers around the sacred enclosure is about to fall into it, especially this matter, which in many souls is the strongest motive toward it. God described adultery (zina) and its ugliness as {an abomination}; that is, a sin that is regarded as exceedingly repugnant in the Sharia, in reason, and in natural disposition (fitar), because it includes audacity against the sanctity owed to God, to the woman, to her family or her husband, and it entails the corruption of the marital bed, the mixing of lineages, and other corruptions. And His saying {and an evil way} means: how evil is the way of one who dares to commit this great sin.

{33} This applies to every soul that God has forbidden to be killed: young and old, male and female, free and slave, Muslim and disbeliever who has a covenant (ʿahd). {Except by right}: such as a life for a life, the married adulterer (al-zānī al-muḥṣan), one who abandons his religion and separates himself from the community (al-tārik li-dīnihi al-mufāriq lil-jamāʿah), and a rebel (al-bāghī) while he is in rebellion, if his rebellion cannot be stopped except by killing. {And whoever is killed wrongfully}; i.e., without right, {We have given his heir}: who is the nearest of his male agnatic relatives (ʿaṣabah) and his inheritors {authority}; i.e., a clear proof for retaliation (qiṣāṣ) against the killer. We have also given him a decreed (qadarī) power over that, and this is when the conditions requiring retaliation are met, such as deliberate aggression (al-ʿamd al-ʿudwān) and equality (al-mukāfa'ah). {But let him not exceed bounds}: the heir {in killing}; for he is {indeed supported}. Exceeding bounds (al-isrāf) is transgressing the limit: either by mutilating the killer, or by killing him with other than the means he used, or by killing someone other than the killer. This verse is evidence that the right to killing (in retaliation) belongs to the heir, so retaliation is not carried out except with his permission, and if he pardons, retaliation is dropped; and that the heir of the slain is aided by God against the killer and whoever helps him, until he is enabled to kill him.

This is Allah's kindness and mercy toward the orphan who has lost his father while still young, unaware of what is good for himself and unable to manage it, in that He commanded his guardians to protect him, to protect his wealth, to look after it, and not to approach it "except in the best manner" (إلاَّ بالتي هي أحسنُ): such as trading with it, not exposing it to dangers, and being keen to make it grow. This continues until the orphan reaches his "full strength" (أشدَّه), meaning his maturity, his intellect, and his sound judgment. When he reaches his full strength, guardianship ends for him, he becomes responsible for himself, and his wealth is handed over to him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you perceive in them sound judgment, then hand over to them their property﴾ [An-Nisa: 6]. And ﴿fulfil the covenant﴾: the covenant you made with Allah, and the covenant you made with people. ﴿Indeed, the covenant will be questioned﴾: that is, you will be held accountable for whether you fulfilled it or not. If you fulfil it, there is a great reward for you; and if you do not, there is a great sin upon you.

{35} This is a command to justice and to giving full measure and weight with equity, without defrauding or diminishing. From the general sense is derived the prohibition of every deception in a price, in a thing priced, or in whatever is contracted upon, and the command to sincere advice and truthfulness in dealings. {That is better}: than its absence, {and better in outcome}; that is, better in its final result. Through it the servant is saved from liabilities, and through it blessing descends.

{36} That is: "Do not follow that of which you have no knowledge. Rather, be certain in everything you say and do; do not assume that it goes by without being for you or against you." {Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of these will be questioned about.} It is therefore fitting for the servant, who knows that he will be questioned about what he said and did, and about how he used his limbs which Allah created for His worship, to prepare an answer for the questioning. This is achieved only by using them in the worship of Allah, sincerely devoting the religion to Him, and restraining them from what Allah, exalted is He, dislikes.

{37} He, exalted is He, says: {And do not walk upon the earth exultantly}; that is, with arrogance, conceit and insolence, being haughty toward the truth and self-aggrandizing over creation. {Indeed, you will not tear the earth apart}: by your doing that, {and you will not reach the mountains in height}: through your arrogance. Rather, you will be contemptible in the sight of Allah, despised by the people, hated and detested, having acquired the worst of characteristics and clothed yourself in the most base of them, without attaining any of what you aspire to.

{38} {All of that}: the things mentioned which Allah has forbidden earlier in His saying: {Do not place with Allah another deity}, and the prohibition of disobedience to parents, and what is joined to these, {its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord}; that is, all of that displeases those who do it and harms them, and Allah, exalted is He, dislikes it and rejects it.

{39} {That} which We have explained and clarified of these magnificent rulings, {is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom}: for wisdom is commanding the best of deeds and noble characteristics, and forbidding the base characteristics and the worst deeds. These deeds mentioned in these verses are of the lofty wisdom which the Lord of the worlds revealed to the Master of the messengers in the most noble of books, so that he would command the best of nations with them. They are therefore of the wisdom which whoever is granted has indeed been granted much good. {40} This is a severe denunciation of those who claimed that God has taken daughters from among His creation, saying: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen for you sons and taken for Himself daughters from the angels?﴾ That is, has He chosen for you the best and the complete portion? ﴿And taken for Himself from the angels females﴾ — since they claimed that the angels are the daughters of God. ﴿Indeed, you utter a great saying﴾ — in it is the greatest audacity toward God, since you attributed to Him a child, which implies need, and the independence of some creatures from Him, and you judged for Him the worse of the two portions, namely females, while He is the One who created you and chose you with males. ﴿Exalted is He far above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verses 45–48:

{45} He, exalted is He, informs about His punishment for those who deny the truth, who reject it and turn away from it: that He places a barrier between them and faith. He says: {And when you recite the Qur'an}, which contains admonition, reminder, guidance, faith, goodness and abundant knowledge; {We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier}: it conceals them from truly understanding it, from realizing its realities, and from submitting to the good to which it calls.

{46} {And We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinnah)}; that is, coverings and veils, so that they do not comprehend the Qur'an with them, but hear it only as a hearing by which the proof is established against them. {And in their ears, deafness (waqr)}; that is, deafness to hearing it. {And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an}: calling to His oneness and forbidding association with Him; {they turn their backs in aversion (nufur)}: due to their intense hatred of it and their love for the falsehood they are upon; as He, exalted is He, says: {And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil, and when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice} (39:45).

{47} {We know best what they listen for (bihi)}; that is, We prevented them from benefiting when hearing the Qur'an because We know that their intentions are evil; they want to find the slightest thing with which to find fault. Their listening is not for the sake of seeking guidance and accepting the truth, but they are determined not to follow it, and whoever is in this state, listening does not benefit him at all. For this reason He says: {When they listen to you, and when they are in secret conference (najwa)}; that is, conferring privately, {when the wrongdoers say}, in their private conference: {You follow only a man bewitched (mashur)}. If this is their wrongful private conference among themselves, and they have built it upon his being bewitched, then they are certain that what he says is of no account, and that he raves and does not know what he is saying.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verse 49–52:

{49} He (Exalted is He) informs us of the speech of those who deny the Resurrection, of their denial of it, and of their considering it far-fetched, when they say: ﴿When we have become bones and crumbled dust, shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ That is, bodies that have decayed. ﴿Shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ That is, such a thing cannot happen, being impossible in their opinion. Thus they were in the utmost ignorance, in that they denied the messengers of God and rejected the signs of God, and they measured the power of the Creator of the heavens and the earth by their own weak and incapable powers. When they saw that this was beyond their ability and that they could not do it, they made God's power to be like theirs. Glory be to Him who made a creature of His creation, who claim that they are people of intellect and understanding, an example of the most manifest and clear ignorance, with the clearest and highest proofs, so that He might show His servants that there is nothing but His guidance and His help, or else destruction and error. ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾

{50–51} For this reason, God commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to these deniers of the Resurrection, in a mocking manner: ﴿Be stones or iron, or a creation of what is greater in your breasts﴾ That is, what is greater (in size) in your chests. This is so that, by their own assumption, they might be safe from the power of God reaching them or His will taking effect upon them. For you cannot escape God in whatever state you are or whatever form you take, and you have no control over yourselves in life or after death. So leave the management and disposal to Him who is All-Powerful over everything and encompasses everything. ﴿Then they will say: "Who will restore us?" Not as an acknowledgment from them of the principle of the Resurrection, but rather this is foolishness on their part and an attempt to defeat (the argument). ﴿Say: "Perhaps it is near."﴾ So there is no benefit in specifying its time; the benefit and the focus lie in establishing it, affirming it, and confirming it. Otherwise, everything that is to come is near.

{52} ﴿The Day He calls you﴾ to the Resurrection and the rising, and the trumpet is blown, ﴿and you will respond with His praise﴾ That is, you will submit to His command and will not disobey Him. His words ﴿with His praise﴾ mean that He is praised for His action, and He will recompense the servants with it when He gathers them for the Day of Mutual Recrimination. ﴿And you will think that you remained but a little while﴾ because of the swiftness of its occurrence, and because the bliss you had passed through will seem as though it had never been. This is what the deniers asked about, saying: "When is it?" They will regret with the utmost regret when it arrives, and it will be said to them: "This is what you used to deny."

{56} God the Exalted says: {Say} to the polytheists who associate others with God, who have taken rivals besides Him, worshipping them as they worship God and calling upon them as they call upon Him, holding them to account to establish what they claim and believe, if they are truthful: {Call upon those you claim} to be gods besides God. Then look: can they benefit you or remove harm from you? For they do not {possess the removal of harm from you}, whether it is sickness, poverty, hardship or the like. They cannot repel it altogether. Nor do they possess its transfer from one person to another, or from one hardship to a lesser one. If they are of this description, then why do you call upon them besides God? For they have no perfection and no beneficial actions, so taking them as gods is a deficiency in religion and in intellect, and foolishness in judgment.

It is strange that foolishness, when it becomes habitual and practised, and is received from misguided forefathers with acceptance, is seen by its owner as sound judgment and beneficial reason, while sincerity of religion toward God, the One, the Unique, the Perfect, who bestows all blessings, outward and inward, is seen as foolishness and a matter to be wondered at. This is what the polytheists said: {Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a wondrous thing!}

{57} Then He informs that those who worship them besides God are preoccupied with something else, occupied with their need of God and their seeking of a means of access to Him. So He said: {Those whom they call upon}, namely the prophets, the righteous and the angels, {seek access to their Lord, [each] of them seeking to be nearer}; that is, they compete in drawing near to their Lord, and they expend whatever good deeds they can that bring them closer to God the Exalted and to His mercy. {And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment}, so they avoid everything that leads to punishment. {Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared}; that is, it is the thing against which one should be exceedingly cautious and guard against its causes. Whoever has them perfected, his affairs are perfected; and when the heart is empty of them, goodness departs from it and evils surround it.

The sign of love is what God mentioned: that the servant strive in every deed that brings him closer to God, compete for nearness to Him by making all deeds sincere for God, giving sincere counsel in them, and performing them in the most perfect manner within his power. Whoever claims to love God without this is a liar.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verses 59–60:

{59} He, exalted is He, mentions His mercy in not sending the signs that the deniers propose, and that He withheld from sending them only out of fear of their denial of them. So if they deny them, punishment hastens upon them and descends on them without delay, as He did with the earlier peoples who denied them. Among the greatest signs is the sign that Allah sent to Thamud, which was the great and dazzling she-camel, from which the entire tribe, all of them, would drink, and yet they denied it, so there befell them what Allah related to us in His Book. These people are likewise: if the great signs came to them, they would not believe, for what prevented them from faith is not the obscurity of what the Messenger brought, or the confusion over whether it is truth or falsehood. Indeed, there has come such abundant evidence proving the soundness of what he brought, which is sufficient to guide whoever seeks guidance; so other signs are like it, and they will necessarily follow with them what they followed with other than them. Therefore, withholding their sending in such a state is better and more beneficial for them. As for His saying: {And We send not the signs except as a warning} – meaning: the purpose of them was not that they should be a summons and a cause for the faith that is attained only through them, but rather the purpose of them is warning and intimidation, so that they may refrain from what they are upon.

{60} {And [recall] when We told you that your Lord had encompassed the people} – in knowledge and power; so they have no refuge to which they can resort, nor any shelter in which they can seek protection from Him. This suffices whoever has intellect to restrain from what Allah dislikes, the One who encompasses the people. {And We did not make the vision which We showed you} – most of the exegetes hold that it is the night of the Isra' (Night Journey). {And the accursed tree} – which is mentioned {in the Qur'an} – is the tree of Zaqqum, which grows at the root of Hellfire.

The meaning: since these two matters became a trial for people, to the point that the disbelievers persisted in their disbelief and their evil increased, and some whose faith was weak turned away from it – because what he informed them of, of matters that occurred on the night of the Isra', and the Isra' from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, was beyond the ordinary, and likewise the report of the existence of a tree growing at the root of Hellfire is also among the extraordinary matters – this is what caused them to deny. So how would it be if they witnessed the great signs and the immense marvels? Is it not more fitting that their evil would increase on account of it? Therefore Allah had mercy on them and turned them away from them. From here you know that the non-explicit mention in the Book and the Sunnah of the great matters that occurred in later times is more appropriate and better, for matters that people have never witnessed a parallel to may not be accepted by their minds if they were informed of them before they occur, so that would become a doubt in the hearts of some believers and an obstacle preventing those who have not entered Islam and repelling them from it. Rather, Allah mentioned general expressions that encompass all that will occur. And Allah knows best. {And We warn them}, with the signs, {but it increases them not except in great transgression} – and this is the most eloquent description of adorning oneself with evil and loving it, hating good and not submitting to it.

**Verse 61**

He, blessed and exalted, alerts His servants to the severity of Satan's enmity and his eagerness to lead them astray. When God created Adam, Satan refused to prostrate to him, and he said, in arrogance: ﴿Shall I prostrate myself before one You created from clay?﴾ That is, from clay. He claimed that he was better than Adam, because he had been created from fire. The corruption of this false analogy (qiyas) has already been explained in several respects.

**Verse 62**

When it became clear to Iblis that God had favored Adam, he said, addressing God: ﴿Tell me, is this the one You have honored above me? If You grant me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants﴾. That is, I will utterly destroy them by misguidance and lead them astray. ﴿Except a few﴾: the wicked one knew that some of them would necessarily oppose him and disobey him.

**Verse 63**

God said to him: ﴿Go, and whoever among them follows you﴾, having chosen you over his Lord and his true Protector. ﴿Indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾; that is, stored up for you, a complete reward for your deeds.

**Verse 64**

Then God commanded him to do everything within his power to lead them astray, and He said: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾. This includes every caller to disobedience. ﴿And muster against them your horse and your foot soldiers﴾. This includes every rider and every walker who is in disobedience to God; they are the cavalry and infantry of Satan. The point is that God has tested the servants with this clear enemy, who calls them to disobey God by his words and deeds. ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾. This encompasses every act of disobedience connected to their wealth and children: withholding zakat (obligatory almsgiving), expiations (kaffarat), and obligatory rights; failing to discipline children and raise them in goodness and to keep them from evil; taking wealth unlawfully, spending it unlawfully, or earning through base means. Indeed, many exegetes have mentioned that sharing with Satan in wealth and children includes neglecting the tasmiyah (saying the name of God) over food, drink, and marital relations; and that if one does not mention the name of God in these, Satan shares in them, as is reported in a hadith. ﴿And make promises to them﴾: flattering promises that have no reality. Hence He said: ﴿Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾; that is, falsehood that vanishes. For example, he makes sins and corrupt beliefs appear attractive to them and promises them reward for them, because they think they are upon the truth. And the Exalted said: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Himself and bounty﴾.

**Verse 65**

Having informed us of what Satan intends to do to the servants, He mentioned what protects against his temptation, which is worship of God and the upholding of faith and reliance upon Him. So He said: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority﴾; that is, no power of domination or misguidance. Rather, God repels every evil from them through their devotion to Him, protects them from the accursed Satan, and suffices them. ﴿And your Lord is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs﴾ for whoever relies upon Him and fulfills what he has been commanded.

{66} He mentions His favor upon the servants through what He subjected for them of ships, boats and vessels. He inspired them in how to build these, and He subjected to them the surging sea, which carries them upon its back, so that the servants might benefit from them in riding, in carrying their loads, and in trade. This is from His mercy toward His servants, for He has always been Merciful and Compassionate toward them, granting them everything in which their wills and benefits are involved.

{67} Among His mercies that show He alone is the one worthy of worship, to the exclusion of all else, is that when harm touches them at sea and they fear destruction because the waves have piled up, those whom they used to call upon besides Allah in times of ease, whether living or dead, fall away from them. It is as though they had never called upon them at any time, because they know that these are weak and incapable of removing harm. They cry out with the call to the Originator of the earth and the heavens, the One whom all creatures seek help from in their hardships, and they devote their supplication and humble entreaty to Him alone in this state. But when Allah removes the harm from them and brings them safely to land, they forget what they used to call upon before, and they associate with Him those who neither benefit nor harm, neither give nor withhold, and they turn away from sincerity toward their Lord and their Sovereign.

This is from the ignorance and disbelief of man, for man is ungrateful for favors, except for those whom Allah guides, bestowing upon them a sound intellect, and who are guided to the Straight Path. Such a person knows that the One who removes hardships and delivers from terrors is the One who deserves to be singled out, and all actions should be sincerely directed to Him, in hardship and ease, in difficulty and comfort. As for one who is forsaken and left to his weak intellect, he, in a time of hardship, takes notice only of his immediate benefit and his deliverance in that state. When deliverance is achieved for him and the hardship is lifted, he thinks, in his ignorance, that he has overcome Allah, and no thought of worldly consequences crosses his heart, let alone matters of the Hereafter.

{68–69} For this reason Allah reminded them with His words: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind of stones?﴾ That is, He is capable of all things. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verses 71–72:

Every nation will be presented, and their messenger who called them will be present with them, and their deeds will be presented upon the Book to which the Messenger calls, whether they conform to it or not. Thus they divide into two categories: ﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾: because he followed his imam, the guide to a straight path, and was guided by his Book, so his good deeds increased and his evil deeds decreased; ﴿they will read their record﴾: reading with joy and delight, according to what they see in it that gladdens and pleases them, ﴿and they will not be wronged the extent of a fibre﴾: in respect of the good deeds they performed.

{72} ﴿And whoever was blind in this﴾: in this world, ﴿blind﴾: to the truth; so he did not accept it, nor submit to it, but followed misguidance, ﴿he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾: unable to take the path to Paradise just as he did not take it in this world, ﴿and more astray in way﴾: for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and as you sow, so shall you reap.

In this verse there is evidence that every nation is called to its religion and its Book, and whether it acted upon it or not; and that they are not held accountable by the law of a prophet whom they were not commanded to follow; and that Allah does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him and he has opposed it; and that the people of good are given their records in their right hands, and there results for them a great deal of joy and delight; and that the people of evil are the opposite of that, and that they will be unable to read their records because of the intensity of their distress, grief and dismay.

In these verses there is evidence of the servant's utter need for Allah's making him firm, and that he [should] never cease to entreat his Lord to keep him steadfast in faith, striving in every means that leads to it; for the Prophet (ﷺ), who was the most perfect of creation, was told by Allah: ﴿Had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little﴾; so how about anyone else?!

And in them: Allah's reminder to His Messenger of His favour upon him and his protection from evil. This indicates that Allah loves that His servants be mindful of His blessings upon them when the causes of evil are present, by being protected from it and remaining steadfast in faith.

And in them: according to the elevation of the servant's rank and the continuous succession of blessings upon him from Allah, his sin becomes greater and his offence is multiplied if he does what he is blamed for; for Allah reminded His Messenger that if he did so, and far be it from him, [then] ﴿We would have made you taste a double portion of life and a double portion of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verse 78–81:

{78} Allah commands His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to establish the prayer completely, both outwardly and inwardly, at its times: {at the decline of the sun} (li-dulūk al-shams); that is, its inclination toward the western horizon after midday (zawal). This includes the Dhuhr prayer and the 'Asr prayer. {Until the darkness of the night} (ilā ghasaq al-layl); that is, its darkness. This includes the Maghrib prayer and the 'Isha' prayer. {And the Qur'an of dawn} (wa-qur'āna al-fajr); that is, the Fajr prayer. It is called "Qur'an" because the recitation in it is legislated to be longer than in other prayers, and because of the merit of its recitation, since Allah, the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it.

In this verse is the mention of the five times of the obligatory prayers, and that the prayers performed within them are obligatory, since they are specified by the command.

In it is also that the time is a condition for the validity of the prayer, and that it is the cause of its obligation, since Allah commanded its establishment at these times. Also, the Dhuhr and 'Asr may be combined, and likewise Maghrib and 'Isha', due to a valid excuse, since Allah has combined their times together.

In it is the virtue of the Fajr prayer, the virtue of lengthening the recitation in it, and that the recitation in it is a pillar (rukn), since when an act of worship is named after one of its parts, this indicates the obligation of that part.

{79} His saying: {And from the night, perform tahajjud with it} (wa-min al-layl fa-tahajjad bihi); that is, pray with it at other times during the night, {as a supererogatory prayer for you} (nāfilatan laka); that is, so that the night prayer becomes an addition for you in elevation of rank and raising of degrees, unlike for others, for whom it becomes an expiation for their misdeeds. It may also be that the meaning is: the five prayers are obligatory upon you and upon the believers, whereas the night prayer is obligatory upon you in particular, due to your honor with Allah, that He made your duty greater than that of others, so that your reward may increase, and so that you attain the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), which is the station in which the first and last generations will praise you: the station of the Great Intercession (al-shafa'a al-'uzma), when the creatures seek intercession from Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, and all of them make excuses and hold back from it, until they seek intercession from the master of the children of Adam, so that Allah may relieve them of the distress and anguish of the standing place. He will intercede with his Lord, and his intercession will be accepted, and He will raise him to a station for which the first and last generations will envy him, and he will have a favor over all creation.

{80} His saying: {And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit} (wa-qul rabbi adkhilnī mudkhala ṣidqin wa-akhrijnī makhraja ṣidqin); that is, make all my entrances and exits in Your obedience and in pursuit of Your pleasure, because these contain sincerity and conformity with the command. {And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority} (wa-ij'al lī min ladunka sulṭānan naṣīrā); that is, a manifest proof and a decisive argument for everything I bring and everything I leave. This is the highest state that Allah bestows upon a servant: that all his conditions be good and bring him closer to his Lord, and that for every state he is in there be a manifest proof. This includes beneficial knowledge and righteous action, through knowledge of the issues and the evidences.

{81} His saying: {And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished} (wa-qul jā'a al-ḥaqqu wa-zahaqa al-bāṭil). The truth (al-ḥaqq) is what Allah revealed to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so Allah commanded him to say and proclaim: the truth has come, against which nothing can stand, and falsehood has vanished; that is, it has been crushed and dissipated. {Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish} (inna al-bāṭila kāna zahūqā); that is, this is the description of falsehood. However, it may have a surge and a currency when the truth does not confront it. But when the truth comes, falsehood is crushed and has no movement left. For this reason falsehood only circulates in times and places devoid of knowledge of the signs and clear proofs of Allah. And His saying:

{82} The Qur'an contains healing and mercy, but this is not for everyone. It is for the believers who affirm it, who accept its verses and have knowledge of it. As for the wrongdoers, who either do not affirm it or do not act upon it, its verses increase them in nothing but loss, since through it the proof is established against them. The healing that the Qur'an contains is general: it heals hearts from doubts, ignorance, corrupt opinions, deviation, evil conduct and wicked intentions, for it contains certain knowledge by which every doubt and ignorance is removed, and admonition and reminder by which every desire that opposes the command of God is removed. It also heals bodies from their pains and sicknesses. As for mercy, it lies in the means and causes that it urges, so that whenever the servant performs them, he attains mercy, eternal happiness, and reward both swiftly and later.

This is the nature of man as such, except for those whom Allah has guided. When Allah bestows blessings upon a person, he rejoices in the favours, becomes elated by them, turns away, and turns his side away from his Lord; so he neither thanks Him nor remembers Him. {And when harm touches him}: such as illness or the like, {he is despairing}: of good, having cut off his hope in his Lord, and he thinks that what he is in will last forever. As for those whom Allah has guided, when blessings come they humble themselves before their Lord and thank Him for His favour, and when adversity comes they beseech Him, and hope from Allah for His well-being and the removal of what has befallen them; and by this the trial becomes lighter for them.

{84} That is: {Say, "Each works according to his manner"}, i.e., according to what befits him of conditions. If they are of the elect, the righteous, then only their deeds for the Lord of the worlds suit them; and whoever is among the others, the forsaken, then only deeds for creatures suit them, and only what accords with their aims agrees with them. And {your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way}: He knows who is fit for guidance so He guides him, and who is not fit for it so He forsakes him and does not guide him.

This passage includes a warning against those who ask questions whose only purpose is to test and embarrass, and who neglect what is important. They ask about the soul (al-ruh), which is among the hidden matters whose nature and modality no one can fully describe, while they are deficient in the knowledge that servants actually need. For this reason, Allah commanded His Messenger to answer their question with His words: ﴿Say, "The soul is of the affair of my Lord"﴾; that is, it is among His creatures which He commanded to be, and so they came to be. Therefore there is no great benefit in asking about it, given your lack of knowledge of other things.

In this verse there is evidence that when a person is asked about a matter, it is better for the questioner, other than the one who answered, to turn away from the answer and direct him to what he needs, and guide him to what will benefit him.

{86–87} He, exalted is He, informs that the Qur'an and the revelation which He sent down to His Messenger are a mercy from Him upon him and upon His servants, and that it is the greatest of blessings in the absolute sense for His Messenger. For the grace of Allah upon him is great, its measure cannot be estimated. So the One who has bestowed it upon you is able to take it away, and then you would not find anyone to return it to you, nor an advocate (wakil) who would intercede on your behalf with Allah concerning it. So rejoice in it, let your eye be comforted by it, and let not the denial of the deniers and the mockery of the astray grieve you; for they were offered the most noble of blessings and they rejected it, due to their insignificance before Allah and His abandonment of them.

{88} This is a decisive proof and a shining demonstration of the truth of what the Messenger brought and of his truthfulness. God challenged mankind and the jinn to produce the like of it, and He informed them that they would not produce its like, even if they all cooperated in doing so; they would not be able to. And it happened as God informed: the motives of his enemies who denied it were abundant to reject what he brought in whatever way possible, and they were people of the tongue and eloquence. Had they had even the slightest capacity or ability to do so, they would have done it. Thus it is known that they submitted with the utmost submission, willingly and unwillingly, and were unable to oppose it. How could a created being made of dust, deficient in every respect, who has no knowledge, power, will, volition, speech, or perfection except from his Lord, be able to oppose the speech of the Lord of the earth and the heavens, who is aware of all hidden things, who possesses absolute perfection, absolute praise, and great glory, whose ink, if the sea were replenished by seven more seas as ink, and all the trees were pens, would run out and the pens would be spent, yet the words of God would not be exhausted? Just as no created being resembles God in His attributes, so His speech is among His attributes in which no one resembles Him; there is nothing like Him in His essence, names, attributes, or actions, blessed and exalted is He. Woe to the one for whom the speech of the Creator became confused with the speech of the created, and who claimed that Muhammad (ﷺ) fabricated it against God and invented it from himself.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 17, verse 89–96:

{89–93} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example﴾; that is, We have varied in it the admonitions and the examples, and repeated in it the meanings that the servants need, so that they may take heed and be mindful [of God]. Yet none took heed except a few of them, those for whom the preceding good fortune from God had been decreed and whom God aided with His success. As for most people, they refused except to disbelieve in this blessing, which is greater than all blessings, and they began to demand from him signs other than His signs, which they invented from their own wrongdoing and ignorant selves. They said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who brought this Qur'an containing every proof and sign: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾; that is, flowing rivers. ﴿Or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes﴾: so that you may be independent of it, walking in the markets and coming and going. ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾; that is, pieces of punishment. ﴿Or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾; that is, all together, or face to face and in plain sight, testifying for you to what you have brought. ﴿Or you have a house of gold﴾; that is, adorned with gold and other things. ﴿Or you ascend into the sky﴾: a physical ascent. ﴿And even with this, we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we may read.﴾ Since these were demands of defiance and impossible challenges, and speech of the most foolish and wrongdoing of people, containing rejection of the truth and bad manners toward God, and [the claim] that the Messenger (ﷺ) is the one who brings the signs, God commanded him to declare Him free of this, so He said: ﴿Say: Glory be to my Lord﴾, exalted far above what you say, and He is far above having His rulings and signs follow their corrupt desires and misguided opinions. ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?﴾: he has no part in the affair.

{94} This is the reason that prevented most people from believing: the messengers sent to them were of their own kind, human beings. This was part of His mercy toward them, that He sent to them a human being from among them, for they could not bear to receive [revelation] directly from the angels.

{95} Had there been in the earth angels walking securely: they would be steadfast in seeing the angels and receiving from them; ﴿We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾: so that they could receive from him.

{96} ﴿Say: God is sufficient as a witness between me and you; indeed He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.﴾ Among His testimony to His Messenger is what He supported him with of miracles, what He sent down to him of signs, and His victory over those who opposed and hostilely confronted him. Had he fabricated some sayings against Him, He would have seized him by the right hand, then severed his aorta; indeed He is Acquainted and Seeing, nothing concealed from Him of the states of His servants.
